comments.author: @RealLifeFilesDoc
comments.text: An island where the ground beneath your feet has 70 colors, women use 'red earth' (Gelak) as a spice on their bread, and the seawater glows at night. No cars, no traffic lights, yet it sits right next to a shipping lane that once carried a fifth of the world's oil. The contrast between the surreal beauty of Hormuz and the bustling world outside is simply unbelievable! Who else wants to taste that 'red dirt' bread now? 🇮🇷🍞

replies.author: @reallifeincountries
replies.text: Hormuz Island is truly mind-blowing! 🌋 🍞 The edible red soil (Gelak) and bioluminescent beaches make it feel like another planet entirely. Thanks for sharing this amazing breakdown!"
